Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(1\right)z=2 \cdot e^{\left(x-6\right)}.$$

$$e^{\left(x-6\right)}z=e^{2 \cdot \left(x-6\right)}+C.$$

Thus

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:
